title: Me actually liking a Shakespeare show?!?  That’s character developmen...
transcript: I saw Kit Connor and Rachel Ziegler in Romeo and Juliet, and I'm gonna be honest, I'm really not a Romeo and Juliet fan. But while I was very excited to see the two of them, I went in with very tempered expectations, because generally, this play really does not do it for me. And this past summer, I went to see the Tom Holland version in London, and I found it to be disastrous. So, like, I've been burned before by celebrity casting in Romeo and Juliet, but I am happy to report that this production does indeed slap. I thought that both Rachel and kit are giving really good performances, especially kit, who I think is the breakout star of this production. Like, he is so perfectly cast as Romeo. The other standout for me was Gabby Beans, who plays Mercutio and the friar. She is one of my favorite up and coming actresses, and she is fantastic in this, as she is in every other show that I've seen her in. I also really love the overall direction of this show, and it felt really young and fresh in a way that not many modern Romeo and Juliet adaptations are able to. One thing I didn't really love about this production was the inclusion of the songs, which were fine on their own, but to me just felt so out of place. It felt like we interrupt this production of Romeo and Juliet to bring you Rachel Zegler singing this song. And don't get me wrong, I love hearing Rachel Ziegler sing, but I just didn't feel like these songs really added much or felt meaningfully integrated. But besides that small nitpick, I think it's really hard to find fault in this production. I would also be remiss if I did not mention that I think of all of the shows I've seen in circle in the square, this one utilizes the space in the best way. Like, I won't spoil anything, but there are scenes that take place around the theater, and I thought that they were all really well done. So all in all, it's going to be a big recommendation from me, which I did not think I would be saying about a production of Romeo and Juliet. It is a limited run and I believe the production is mostly sold out, but there may be a ticket still left here or there. And they also have a digital lottery and an in person rush, so check it out if you can!
reasoning: The reviewer clearly recommends the production despite not being a fan of Romeo and Juliet generally. He praises the leads (especially Kit Connor), the direction, the use of the theater space, and calls it a 'big recommendation.' However, he has a notable caveat about the songs feeling out of place, which tempers the enthusiasm slightly below rave territory.
